config_dir.strict_note: if the variable is set the directory must already exist, or Codex errors out

*.note: same path on darwin, linux and win32 — no XDG, no %APPDATA%. Only when Codex is in its default 'file' mode; see 'requires'.

requires.note: 'keyring' keeps the login in the OS keyring (an encrypted file plus a keyring passphrase on Windows) and never reads auth.json; 'auto' prefers the keyring and deletes auth.json after a successful save; 'ephemeral' keeps it in memory. Requirements outrank the user's config, which outranks the system's. Not visible from here: macOS managed preferences, an enterprise cloud bundle, a --profile file, a project's .codex/config.toml and -c on the command line.

companion_note: none — auth.json is self-contained, so there is no splice step and no way for identity and token to desynchronize

policy.rotates_note: a snapshot taken before a refresh is DEAD; the old refresh token was invalidated by the rotation. Profiles must be re-stashed after use, not only on switch-away.

provenance.source: github.com/openai/codex at c0cc9fc (2026-11-12): codex-rs/login/src/auth/storage.rs, codex-rs/utils/home-dir/src/lib.rs, codex-rs/config/defaults.toml, codex-rs/config/src/loader/mod.rs

surfaces_note: all three share one auth.json. Desktop sharing is strong inference, not documented: ChatGPT.app bundles the identical binary and keeps its non-credential state in ~/.codex

token.note: emptied in place when the login is cleared, as with Claude
